prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1477; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received from the policyholder reporting a low-speed collision while the insured vehicle was parked and stationary in a supermarket lot. The claimant, who was in the vehicle at the time, has retained counsel, and all contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Assigned the file and requested the police report, which has been received and records the claimant as an occupant of the vehicle at the scene. The responding officer's account matches the reported location and the general sequence of events.

Entry 3: Spoke with the policyholder, who confirmed the driver lives in the household and is listed as a covered household member under the policy. The policyholder had no knowledge of any prior damage to the vehicle.

Entry 4: Reviewed the photographs submitted by the driver, which show damage to the rear bumper and tailgate consistent with a rear impact. Some details in the photos line up with the reported account, though no independent witnesses have come forward.

Entry 5: Obtained a repair estimate from the authorized body shop. The damage is largely in line with the described impact, and the shop found no sign of older repair work or pre-existing deterioration in the affected panels.

Entry 6: Checked the vehicle history and prior claims records. No earlier damage to the vehicle appears in any source, and nothing suggests the damage predates the policy inception date.

Entry 7: Received the claimant's medical records through counsel. A concussion diagnosis was documented after the incident, and the injury appears consistent with the kind and force of a collision of this type.

Entry 8: Reviewed the medical history with the claimant's authorization. No earlier injury to the same body area is recorded, and no prior treatment for head or neck complaints is known.

Entry 9: Treatment followed a usual course, with initial evaluation, follow-up visits, and gradual reduction in care as symptoms improved. The treating provider's notes describe steady recovery over the period.

Entry 10: Spoke with counsel about the claimant's account. The claimant has described the events the same way in every conversation so far, and the details have not shifted between the initial report and later interviews.

Entry 11: Reviewed the file with the claims supervisor. The police record, the vehicle damage, and the medical findings are consistent with one another, and no additional investigation appears necessary at this stage.

Entry 12: Set the file for routine follow-up with counsel to confirm final treatment status and to request any remaining bills before the injury evaluation is completed.
